stories.headline: UN-backed reports warn conflict is driving acute hunger and instability across multiple regions
stories.summary: A UN News brief carried by Global Issues says more than 26.5 million people in the Democratic Republic of Congo face acute hunger, with eastern conflict displacing millions and aid reaching only a fraction of those targeted. The same roundup notes Taliban corporal punishments in Afghanistan and a UNEP warning that global sand extraction is outpacing natural replenishment.
stories.pastoral_note: Pray with a wide lens today: not just for headlines to calm down, but for the hungry, displaced, silenced, and forgotten to be seen by God’s people.

stories.headline: Christians killed in renewed Plateau State attacks in Nigeria
stories.summary: Morning Star News reports that Fulani assailants killed 13 Christians in Bassa County, Plateau State, on May 8, following earlier raids in the region that killed 11 Christians across three villages. The report says a pastor and family were slain in a prior attack, underscoring the continuing vulnerability of Christian communities in Nigeria’s Middle Belt.
stories.pastoral_note: This is a sober reminder to lead intercession beyond our own church concerns: the body of Christ is one body, and some members worship under threat.

stories.headline: Younger generations show signs of pushing back against doomscrolling
stories.summary: A Mastercard study highlighted a shift among Gen Z and Gen Alpha from passive scrolling toward agency, micro-communities, and digital self-care. The report cites GWI research saying 40% of 12- to 15-year-olds worldwide take breaks from screen time for digital wellbeing.
stories.pastoral_note: There may be a discipleship opening here: young people are not only addicted to screens; many are hungry for boundaries, embodied community, and practices that give them back their attention.

stories.headline: Tech companies turn to faith leaders in search of AI ethics
stories.summary: AP reports that representatives from companies including Anthropic and OpenAI met with religious leaders in New York for an inaugural Faith-AI Covenant roundtable. The initiative seeks moral norms for AI, while critics warn that faith consultation must not become a substitute for real accountability.
stories.pastoral_note: The church should not be naive about Silicon Valley motives, but neither should we miss the moment: public ethics is asking religious questions again, even if it does not know how to name them.

stories.headline: HBR asks whether leaders should treat AI like a teammate
stories.summary: Harvard Business Review’s leadership page features a May 12 piece, “Should You Treat AI Like a Teammate?”, noting renewed leadership questions about AI agents, coworker dynamics, and organizational judgment. The topic points to the next management challenge: not merely adopting tools, but defining responsibility, trust, and human oversight.
stories.pastoral_note: For church leadership, the same question applies spiritually: tools can assist ministry, but they cannot carry calling, character, discernment, or shepherding love.

stories.headline: Fraser Valley housing market shows early signs of stabilization
stories.summary: The Fraser Valley Real Estate Board’s April 2026 market report says benchmark prices edged upward for a second consecutive month, while sales rose both month-over-month and year-over-year for the first annual increase in more than a year. Inventory remains elevated, keeping conditions balanced and favourable for buyers.
stories.pastoral_note: Housing pressure remains a pastoral reality in the Fraser Valley: beneath market language are young families, renters, seniors, and newcomers trying to discern stability and stewardship.

stories.headline: Great Green Wall shows slow but tangible progress in Nigeria and the Sahel
stories.summary: Inter Press Service reports that Africa’s Great Green Wall initiative is showing slow, steady gains in places like northern Nigeria, where tree planting is helping reduce destructive winds, retain soil moisture, and restore livelihoods. The wider initiative aims to restore degraded land, create jobs, and strengthen food and water security across the Sahel.
stories.pastoral_note: This is a small resurrection sign: faithful, earthy work—planting trees, tending land, rebuilding livelihoods—can become hope with roots.

stories.headline: Anxious young adults in China turn to fortunetelling, revealing a hunger for guidance
stories.summary: Christianity Today reports that economic uncertainty and personal anxiety are fueling renewed interest in horoscopes, palm reading, feng shui, fortunetelling bars, and AI-powered divination among Chinese young people. Christian leaders warn against divination while also seeing the search for transcendence as a potential doorway to Jesus.
stories.pastoral_note: The evangelistic edge is clear: when people seek control over the future, the church can offer more than predictions—we bear witness to the Father who knows, guides, and holds tomorrow.
